comment_body:
The cmd.exe branch cannot uphold the documented “single, literal argument” contract: it silently deletes valid double quotes, and `%NAME%` (plus `!NAME!` when delayed expansion is enabled) still expands inside the resulting quotes. It is also unsafe for multiline generated messages because `Terminal.sendText` converts embedded newlines to Enter presses, while cmd.exe does not continue an unmatched double-quoted command. Route cmd.exe messages to the repository input box instead of emitting a lossy command.

This issue also appears on line 26 of the same file.

@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ *  Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.
+ *  Licensed under the MIT License. See License.txt in the project root for license information.
+ *--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+
+/**
+ * Quotes a value so a shell passes it along as a single, literal argument.
+ *
+ * Single quotes are preferred over double quotes because they suppress variable expansion
+ * and command substitution outright, instead of relying on every special character (`$`,
+ * a backtick, a backslash) being individually escaped.
+ *
+ * @param value The value to quote.
+ * @param shell The detected shell, from `vscode.TerminalState.shell`. Shells that are unknown
+ * or not listed fall back to POSIX rules.
+ */
+export function quoteShellArgument(value: string, shell: string | undefined): string {
+	switch (shell) {
+		case 'pwsh':
+			// A single-quoted PowerShell string is literal; an embedded ' is escaped by doubling it.
+			return `'${value.replace(/'/g, `''`)}'`;
+		case 'cmd':
+			// cmd.exe quotes only with double quotes and has no escape character inside them, so
+			// an embedded " cannot be represented and is dropped rather than split the argument.
+			return `"${value.replace(/"/g, '')}"`;

comment_body: After this error path, the broken image keeps its `src`. A later teleport calls `_startRespawnEffectAnimation`, sees the same source, and because `naturalWidth` is still zero it neither starts an animation nor fires another load/error event, leaving `_hostTransition` in `despawning` forever. Clear the source here (or otherwise force a retry) before finishing the transition.

This error event is asynchronous and can belong to a teleport that has already been retargeted. If the current destination is a `fall` host by the time it fires, `_finishHostTransition()` aborts that unrelated fall. Gate cleanup to the current teleport transition (or associate the image request with a transition generation).

This call is outside the `try/finally`, but `installWindowsApp` can throw after the installer has run while validating the installed executable. In that case the new shortcut installation is left behind, contrary to the cleanup guarantee and potentially breaking subsequent sanity runs; move installation into a cleanup scope or make the install helper roll back on post-install validation failures.

Returning here drops the current horizontal offset for a lazily created editor. The caller's autorun tracks only `scrollLeft` and the binding; expanding an already-bound collapsed item creates the editor without changing either dependency, so the autorun does not call this method again. If the multi-diff is already horizontally scrolled, the newly expanded row remains at scroll-left 0 until another horizontal scroll event. Cache the offset and apply it in `_createEditor`, or make the caller observe `editorObservable`.

`unusedCount` is the total pool size, not the number of templates in the same weight class. After collapsed scrolling fills the pool with header-only templates, an editor-bearing template is disposed whenever the total is already at least five. Scrolling expanded files will therefore rebuild editors repeatedly until the header pool drains below five, rather than retaining the previous five reusable editors. Please track lightweight and editor-bearing entries separately, evicting a lightweight entry when necessary to admit up to five editor templates.

comment_body: This override also matches non-code `<pre>` elements, including raw HTML emitted by the Markdown engine (`html: true`) and the frontmatter error `<pre>`. Because only a direct `<code>` child receives the replacement scrolling rule below, long content in those elements now overflows the preview instead of remaining scrollable. Scope the overflow change to code-block containers, for example by adding a dedicated class to `pre` when the copy button is injected and selecting that class here.

This new required service is not registered by `src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/sessions/sessionsTitleBarWidget.fixture.ts`. That fixture directly creates `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel`, so resolving this constructor now fails before its title-bar screenshots can render. Register a no-op `IAgentHostFilterService` there (with `onDidChange = Event.None` and no selected host), as the other Sessions fixtures do.

When `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled` is turned off, the entry remains in `IRemoteAgentHostService.configuredEntries` while the entry-driven contributions remove its provider (`_getProviderEntries` returns no entries when disabled). This condition then synthesizes the old selected host, leaving a connectable picker row with no provider; reconnecting can dial the host but the contribution will not recreate its provider while the setting is off. Gate this retention on the enabled state, or clear the retained host when providers are intentionally disabled.

The Windows packaging task copies the checked-in `build/win32/inno_updater.exe` (see `build/gulpfile.vscode.win32.ts:142-146`), and that binary is unchanged in this PR, so the generated installers will still contain the old updater and this issue will not be fixed. Deleting the entry here deterministically breaks the failed-open path for `CustomEditorInput`: this rejection handler is attached before the `tryRetain()` handler, so it deletes the entry before `resolveWebview` catches the model error and returns. `CustomEditorInput.resolve()` then calls `tryRetain()` again and `assertReturnsDefined` throws `Argument is undefined or null`, replacing the extension's error with a generic assertion. Please update that resolve path to tolerate the missing entry (or propagate the original model failure) as part of this change.

This issue also appears on line 71 of the same file.

`hasError` only recognizes input/output details with `isError`, so ordinary tool failures are still hidden. For example, the built-in ask-questions tool can throw, and `LanguageModelToolsService` records that as `toolResultError` without creating `toolResultDetails` unless `alwaysDisplayInputOutput` is enabled; `didExecuteTool` then reaches `Completed` with no details, making this condition suppress the only error row. Preserve the tool-result error on the invocation/serialized state and include it in this check (and add a regression using `toolResultError` alone).

This branch now creates only one tool, but Not Verbose intentionally keeps a singleton as a standalone `ChatToolInvocationPart`. As a result `next` at line 4113 is undefined and this newly added test fails (as noted in the PR description). Make this branch add a second tool so the test actually exercises a group handoff, or change the assertions to cover the singleton path.

The remote server dependency is still pinned to the old unstable SDK in `remote/package.json` and `remote/package-lock.json`. Remote packaging calls this helper against `remote/node_modules` (`build/gulpfile.reh.ts:362`), so it will install/materialize the old platform package and then fail this new `copilot-sdk/index.js` requirement (the old package uses `sdk/index.js`). Please bump both remote manifests to `1.0.15-preview.2` as well.

comment_body: `refreshSessionGitState()` resolves even when its Git probe fails (and also when it discards the result because the primary working directory changed), leaving the previous metadata intact. Reading `branchName` immediately afterward can therefore treat a stale value as freshly validated: a targetless session may capture the wrong target, while a targeted session may be disabled for a branch change that was never confirmed. Please make the refresh expose whether it produced current state, or perform an authoritative branch read here, and only capture/disable after successful validation.

The refreshed state is re-read here before `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest` and the GitHub subscription awaits complete. A configuration-only `setEnabled(..., overrides)` call can finish during that await, but this evaluation then keeps the old `agentMerge`/configuration through `evaluateAgentMerge` and the repair-turn authorization, so it can start work using options the user just disabled (for example, still fixing CI). Re-read or validate the live Agent Merge state after the asynchronous attach/subscription step before acting.

Fixed in 8e2452f84c6. Target capture and rejection now use a strict, authoritative branch query, including after PR attachment, instead of treating refresh completion as proof that cached metadata is current. Failed probes follow the logged retry path; results for a changed working directory are discarded, and successful detached-HEAD reads remain distinct from failures. Added regressions for stale metadata, failed/discarded refreshes, interrupted recovery, and real-Git branch/detached/error behavior.

AI Review: A later stop can be lost while enablement waits for Git. Starting from persisted `enabled: false`, suspend `setEnabled(chatA, true, { mergePullRequest: 'always' })`, then await `setEnabled(chatB, false)` in another chat sharing the folder. The stop reports disabled but performs no write, so these comparisons still pass and the earlier call re-enables monitoring and automatic merging. Please invalidate pending enables on every stop, including no-op stops, or serialize updates per folder. Add a regression starting from persisted disabled state; the new interruption test starts from absent state and misses this case.

AI Review: Enabling during a foreground turn with an already-cached PR now persists both target and PR before that turn ends. Configuration injection correctly waits while busy, but `_completeTurn` only schedules evaluation. With the target already bound, evaluation skips the idle configuration write that previously triggered reconciliation. A base/head probe starts the first repair in `interactive` with manual approvals here, versus `autopilot`/`assisted` on the base when policy permits, so unattended repairs can stall. The subsequent lifecycle write is too late because the repair is active. Please reconcile deferred configuration while idle before claiming the repair, and cover mid-turn enablement with a cached PR.

AI Review: `mergePullRequest: 'never'` still allows autonomous repairs that commit and push changes: `addressReviews`, `fixCI`, and `resolveConflicts` all default to true. This new 'Monitoring only' summary appears in collapsed notices, accessible labels, and completed-tool status while the repair details are hidden. Please use 'Automatic merge is off.' here, or reserve 'Monitoring only' for configurations with every repair action disabled.

The scoped filter only applies to already-tracked terminals. If none exist, the fallback below still adopts any untracked terminal with the same cwd—including a terminal from another Agent Host—and line 378 then relabels it with this host's address. Apply the scope filter to fallback candidates too so a session cannot run commands on another backend.

When two chats share this folder, the enabled folder state is advertised by both chats even though `AgentMergeFolderState.chat` identifies only one owner. The non-owning chat then gets an Agent Merge changeset whose compare template follows the wrong transcript. Please apply the same owning-chat resolution used by `AgentMergeController._resolveOwningChat` before advertising the entry.

The feedback IDs were loaded and accepted under `state.sessionResource`, but this call asks `AgentFeedbackService` to read and mark them under `state.chatResource`. Its backend is keyed by the supplied resource (`getFeedback(sessionResource)`), so the combined action sends no feedback attachment and leaves the session-scoped comments accepted rather than submitted. The API needs separate feedback-scope and target-chat resources.

This issue also appears on line 499 of the same file.

Offscreen rows are cached at the short height here, but scrolling them into view does not rerun this autorun. Rendering also initializes `hadFolderRow` from the already-loaded workspace, so it does not fire `onDidChangeItemHeight`; a chat with a folder badge can therefore render into a row that is one line too short. Reconcile the full height when a row becomes rendered/visible (without eagerly reading offscreen workspaces).

AI Review: Task and manually created terminals do not get a tracked scope. When an automatic terminal already exists, switching away and back reuses it without discovering those extra terminals. This branch then rejects them even for the local __local__ host, leaving their tabs/output hidden while their processes continue running. The base/head probe restores them only on the base. Could we register their backend/folder ownership or provide a backend-aware fallback, with a session round-trip test covering an automatic terminal plus a task terminal?

AI Review: This fallback also runs when workingDirectoryKeys explicitly distinguishes file:///work/API from file:///work/api on a case-sensitive host. If only API has GitHub metadata, for example because api has no GitHub remote, looking up api returns API's repository and PRs: uniqueness is checked only among populated githubData entries. Could we skip the case-insensitive fallback when the host supplied a key for the requested directory, and test two case-distinct folders with GitHub state for only one?

Yes. Here is the condensed strategy:
 * Register Scope: Attach backendId and workspaceFolderUri metadata during manual and task terminal creation so they carry explicit ownership tags.
 * Backend-Aware Fallback: When reconciling sessions, match untracked terminals using their backendId + workspaceFolderUri before discarding them.
 * Probe Parity: Update the head probe to query backend processes using the same workspace and backend filters as the base probe.
 * Round-Trip Test: Initialize an automatic and task terminal, switch workspace context away, switch back, and assert that both tabs re-bind to the UI with running processes intact.
